title: Frontline Heroism and Zada trigger on the same cast

you: Goblin token 1 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Goblin token 2 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Goblin token 3 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Mountain x1 (tapped to cast Crimson Wisps)

scenario.mana_available: {0} (the {R} to cast Crimson Wisps is already paid; no other mana source)

stack.note: cast targeting only Zada, Hedron Grinder

extras.note_for_the_resolver: Both Zada's and Frontline Heroism's abilities trigger on this one cast; you control both triggers and choose their order on the stack.
extras.timing: It is your precombat main phase, you are the active player, and the stack was empty when you cast Crimson Wisps (cost {R}, already paid). It has just become cast and is on the stack; any abilities that triggered on casting it have not yet been put on the stack.

scenario.question: Crimson Wisps is cast targeting only Zada, with Frontline Heroism on the battlefield, and both Zada's and Frontline Heroism's abilities trigger. If you put Zada's trigger on the stack first so Frontline Heroism's resolves first, does the Soldier token it creates exist when Zada's trigger resolves, and so receive a copy of its own? Does the copy Frontline Heroism creates trigger Zada or Frontline Heroism again? How many cards do you draw in total under that order, and under the opposite order?

steps.action: Crimson Wisps is cast targeting only Zada, Hedron Grinder, paying its cost {R} with the one {R} available. It becomes cast and both cast triggers trigger at that moment: Zada's (an instant targeting only Zada) and Frontline Heroism's second ability (a spell that targets only a single creature you control).
steps.effect: Your mana pool is now empty. Two triggered abilities you control are waiting to go on the stack, above Crimson Wisps.

steps.action: Before you receive priority, state-based actions are checked (none apply) and the two triggers are put on the stack. You control both, so you choose their order. ORDER A (the question's order): Zada's trigger first, Frontline Heroism's trigger on top of it.
steps.effect: Stack, bottom to top: Crimson Wisps (targeting Zada), Zada trigger, Frontline Heroism trigger.

steps.action: ORDER A: all players pass; Frontline Heroism's trigger (top) resolves.
steps.effect: You create a 1/1 red Soldier creature token with haste, then copy Crimson Wisps. Frontline Heroism names a new target for the copy, the Soldier, so the copy is put on top of the stack targeting the Soldier, not Zada, above Zada's trigger. The Soldier is now a creature you control on the battlefield. The CR's own worked example for this rule is Frontline Heroism.

steps.action: Does the Frontline copy trigger Zada or Frontline Heroism? No.
steps.effect: The copy was put onto the stack, not cast, so neither cast trigger triggers. (The official Frontline Heroism ruling of 2024-11-08 agrees: its copy is not cast and does not retrigger cast triggers.)

citations.quote: a copy of a spell isn’t cast and a copy of an activated ability isn’t activated.
Any abilities that trigger when a spell is cast or put onto the stack trigger at this time.

steps.action: ORDER A: priority returns; all pass; the Wisps copy targeting the Soldier resolves.
steps.effect: The Soldier is a legal target. It becomes red and gains haste until end of turn, and you draw a card. Resolving puts the copy into a graveyard, where it immediately ceases to exist as a state-based action before anyone gets priority (step 9 gives the rules). Draws so far: 1.

steps.action: ORDER A: all pass; Zada's trigger resolves. 'Each other creature you control that the spell could target' is counted now, at resolution, not when it triggered.
steps.effect: Other creatures you control that Wisps could target: Goblin tokens 1, 2 and 3 and the Soldier, 4 in all. Each is a legal target, so one copy is created for each, targeting that creature, and you put them on the stack in any order, above the original. So yes: the Soldier exists and gets a copy of its own. None of the copies is cast, so nothing triggers again. (The Zada ruling of 2018-03-16 agrees that you choose the order.)

steps.effect: Each Goblin and the Soldier becomes red and gains haste. You draw 4 cards. As each copy finishes resolving it is put into a graveyard and then ceases to exist (step 9). Draws so far: 5.

Your graveyard therefore holds only the one Crimson Wisps card.

steps.effect: When Zada's trigger resolves, the other creatures you control are only Goblin tokens 1-3; the Soldier does not exist yet. So 3 copies, each targeting a different Goblin, go on the stack above Frontline's trigger. They resolve for 3 draws, and each copy then ceases to exist.

steps.effect: The Soldier is created. The copy targeting it resolves (1 draw), then the original resolves on Zada (1 draw). The Soldier never gets a Zada copy because Zada's trigger had already resolved. ORDER B TOTAL: 5 cards (3 + 1 + 1).

final_state.summary: Order the triggers so Frontline Heroism resolves FIRST (put Zada's trigger on the stack first). The Soldier then exists when Zada's trigger resolves and gets its own copy, because Zada counts creatures at resolution (608.2h). Order A: 6 cards. Order B (Zada resolves first): 5 cards. Neither the Frontline copy nor any Zada copy is cast, so neither triggers anything again (707.10). One opponent at 40, no life change. The one {R} was spent casting Wisps, and every copy ceased to exist after resolving, so the graveyard holds only the original card. Assumption: your library holds at least 6 cards. A draw from an empty library is a state-based loss (704.5b), so a smaller library changes the outcome.

you.mana_available: none (the one {R} paid for Crimson Wisps, step 1)

assumptions: Your library holds at least 6 cards (5 under Order B). Under 704.5b, a player who attempted to draw from an empty library since state-based actions were last checked loses the game.
